raw_response:
I’m thinking about it the way I would on my own land. I’ve only farmed independently for 2 years, so I still look a lot at what nearby farmers do, and I listen when the extension guy says something useful, but in the end I can’t gamble too much because my land is only 10.1 mu and there are just 3 people in the household. This year I’ll keep the land spread out: eggplant is still my main cash crop, chili gives another cash stream, and I’ll keep some wheat-maize rotation for steadier yield and to avoid putting everything into vegetables. With well water I can irrigate when needed, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too often unless the crop is at a key stage. For fertilizer, I usually don’t dare cut too low, because if the crop goes yellow or weak, the yield loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also won’t chase very high rates because cash has to stay in hand.

For eggplant, I’ll put the better-managed plot there because it needs more labor and more topdressing through the season. Chili is a bit lighter than eggplant but still a cash crop, so I’ll keep a moderate area. Wheat I’ll manage in the usual local way, then right after harvest I’ll put in summer maize on the same 3.1 mu. The wheat-maize land gives me something more stable, while the vegetables bring in cash if the market is decent. That feels safer for my family than pushing all 10.1 mu into one crop.
